mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day period.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the subsequent month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-rate hike periods (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for 30 consecutive days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (implied via UNRATE) signal a weakening labor market, which increases perceived equity risk and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained PAYEMS increases and UNRATE declines (p < 0.05 two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (implied by GDPC1) during the current quarter predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market anticipates sustained demand.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with GDPC1 acceleration (Pearson's rho < 0.2, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 index for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness that elevates equity risk premia, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 100 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from average during non-contraction periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%, it triggers a risk-on sentiment that lifts S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not exceed the 95th percentile of the pre-3% MA period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (implied by a proxy such as HOUST) while unemployment remains low signals a tight labor market, which can precede equity market stress and drive negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% in a single month while UNRATE remains < 5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained HOUST growth (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (implied by a proxy such as CPIAUCSL decline) suggest weakening consumer demand, which elevates equity risk and results in negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL shows two consecutive monthly declines
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during periods of stable CPIAUCSL (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary policy uncertainty (detected via a composite of FEDFUNDS volatility and CPIAUCSL volatility), S&P 500 20-day forward returns tend to be negative as investors demand a higher risk premium.
candidate_trigger: Variance(FEDFUNDS) > 0.5% and Variance(CPIAUCSL) > 1% for the next 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline uncertainty periods (p > 0.05).
